transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, um... I'm here because, well, after my shifts—I work as a cashier over at the big grocery store on 5th. Which, honestly, has been an absolute nightmare lately because they keep messing with our schedules and my manager, Dave, he just doesn't know how to run a floor at all. We were short-staffed three days in a row last week. 

But anyway, after I finally clock out, I just keep buying these huge takeout orders. Like, I'll go and order enough burgers, fries, chicken, and desserts for an entire family. And the drive-thru lines are always so crazy long at that time, especially on Tuesdays when they do those half-price specials. People just sit there in their cars not moving, staring at their phones, and it drives me crazy... but yeah, I'll get all that food and just sit there and eat almost all of it myself before I even go home. I just... I don't really know why I'm doing it.
Do you usually feel stressed, anxious, or upset before buying and eating all that food?

I don't know, honestly. I haven't really paid attention to how I'm feeling right before I do it. I mean, my feet usually hurt a lot, if that counts? Standing on that terrible tile floor all day really does a number on you, especially because I bought these cheap work shoes from that discount place by the highway. The guy there told me they were memory foam, but I swear it's just cardboard. And you really need good shoes when you're dealing with spills at the store—like the other day, this kid just shattered a whole jar of marinara sauce in aisle three and the mom didn't even tell anybody, just walked away. I almost busted my knee slipping on it when I was trying to grab some receipt paper from the back. 

But, uh... what were you asking? Oh, right, stressed. Yeah, I don't really know if I feel upset or anxious before I go to the drive-thru. I'm not really sure what I'm feeling, it's all just kind of a blur.
Do you think you're eating all that food to try and feel better about something?

To feel better? I mean... I guess I've never really thought about it like that. I don't really know if I'm trying to fix a mood or anything. The food does taste good, mostly. Though, actually, they just changed the buns on the burgers at that place. They used to be these really soft sesame seed ones, and now they're doing that weird shiny brioche stuff. 

My buddy Mike—he works at the auto shop just down the street from the grocery store—he was just complaining about the exact same thing the other day. He was fixing up this old Honda, and we were talking about how everything is just getting way more expensive but the quality keeps going down. Like, even the napkins they hand you at the drive-thru window are paper-thin now. You need like a whole stack of them just to wipe the grease off your hands, and half the time the teenager working the window doesn't even put them in the bag unless you ask. And don't even get me started on how they hoard the ketchup packets now, you have to practically beg for more than two... 

But wait, what were we talking about? Oh, if I eat it to feel better. Yeah, I honestly don't know. I just kind of do it.
Do you think you're eating all that food because of how you're feeling after work?

Because of how I feel after work? I mean... I guess I'm just tired? Usually I just want to get to my car and leave. Which, by the way, is its own kind of torture right now because the AC in my Corolla just went out again. It's a 2012, so I guess I can't complain too much, but man, sitting in that afternoon traffic on the highway with no air conditioning is absolutely brutal. The sun just bakes you right through the windshield. 

I actually tried buying one of those little plastic fans that plugs into the cigarette lighter, you know? But the cord is way too short, so it just sits in the cup holder and blows warm air directly at my knees. It's completely useless. And my mechanic—not Mike, the other guy I go to, Tony—he said it's the compressor, which is gonna cost me like six hundred bucks to fix. Who has six hundred bucks just lying around right now? Especially on what they pay us at the store. I'd have to pick up like five extra shifts just to cover it, and Dave would never approve the overtime anyway. 

But, um... yeah, I don't really know if it's because of a specific feeling. I just get off work, get in my boiling hot car, and then... I just end up at the drive-thru ordering all that stuff. I really couldn't tell you if a feeling is causing it.
Do you think you're eating all that food because you're feeling emotional after work?

Emotional? I mean, I don't really know what you mean by that. I'm just regular tired, you know? Like I said, the store just drains you. Especially when you get stuck on the express lane. People act like they can't read the giant sign that says "15 items or less." I had this one lady yesterday who rolled up with a cart completely full to the brim. She had to have at least fifty things in there, and she just starts unloading it like it's no big deal. And of course, she's got all these coupons that are expired, and she wants to argue with me about every single one. 

And Dave, my manager, he just stands there pretending not to see it happening. He's always doing that. He'll be "checking inventory" on his little clipboard right next to the registers, but the second a customer starts yelling, he suddenly has to go check the back room. It's ridiculous. He actually told me last week that my scan rate was too slow. My scan rate! Like it's my fault the barcode on the store-brand frozen peas is always printed all weird and won't scan on the first try. 

But, uh... emotional? Yeah, I don't think so. I don't really notice feeling anything specific like that. I just go from the store, to the car, to the food. That's just how it happens.
Do you feel like you can stop eating once you've started on those large takeout orders?

Stop? No, not really. It's like... once I take that first bite, it feels like something in me just clicks off. I'll literally be sitting there telling myself, 'Demetrius, stop, you don't need any more,' but my hands just keep reaching for the next thing. 

The next wrapper, the next box... which, by the way, those new cardboard boxes they use for the fries now? They are impossible to break down for the recycling bin. And the city just switched our trash pickup to this new automated truck system where the mechanical arm grabs the bin, right? So they gave us all these new blue recycling carts, but the lids are incredibly flimsy. If the wind blows even a little bit, the lid flips open and all your stuff just blows all over the street. 

Last Tuesday, I spent twenty minutes chasing my own garbage down the block because the truck came by and half the stuff missed the hopper. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she was just standing on her porch watching me. She's got this little yappy terrier mix that never stops barking, and I swear the dog was judging me. She never even offered to help, just stood there holding her watering can. I'm pretty sure she waters her plastic yard flamingos, I swear to God... 

But, um, what were you asking? Oh, stopping. Yeah, no, I can't stop. My hands just keep going until it's all gone.
Do you feel guilty after eating all that food by yourself?

Guilty? I mean... not really? I don't know if guilt is the right word. I usually just feel really stuffed and kind of numb, honestly. I just end up laying there on my couch. Which, man, I really need to get a new couch. The springs on the left side are completely shot. I bought it off Craigslist like five years ago from this guy who lived up on the fourth floor of this ancient apartment building, and let me tell you, trying to pivot that giant sectional down four flights of narrow stairs was an absolute nightmare. 

My buddy Craig was supposed to help me move it, but he bailed at the last minute because he said his truck wouldn't start. Craig's truck is always breaking down, I swear. It's an old Chevy, and he acts like it's the greatest vehicle ever made, but I'm telling you, he spends more time under the hood than he does actually driving the thing. He actually tried to convince me to buy one a few weeks ago when my Corolla was acting up, but I told him there's no way I'm buying a money pit like that. Plus, have you seen gas prices right now? Forget about it. The station down the street from my apartment jumped another fifteen cents just since Tuesday. 

But, uh... what were we talking about? Oh, feeling guilty. Yeah, no, I don't really get like, a guilty feeling about the food. I just feel super full and end up falling asleep.
Do you think eating all that food helps you deal with the frustrations you experience at work?

Help me deal with it? I guess... maybe? I mean, I don't really think about it like it's a tool or something. It's just what I do when I get home. But speaking of tools, I had to buy a new wrench set the other day because the pipes under my kitchen sink started leaking. Just out of nowhere, this steady drip, drip, drip right onto the particle board at the bottom of the cabinet. And of course, the landlord is completely useless. I called him three times, left voicemails, and he finally texts me back saying he's 'out of town' and I should just put a bucket under it. 

A bucket! Like I'm supposed to just live with a bucket of dirty dishwater under my sink for a week. So I went down to the hardware store, the one over on 4th Street, not the big chain one, but the local place. The guy who runs it, Sal, he's been there forever. He knows exactly where every single screw and washer is in that whole store. It's wild. But he was telling me that the city's water pressure has been fluctuating because they're doing construction on the main line down by the highway. 

They've had that highway torn up for, what, six months now? The traffic is a nightmare. You try to take the exit for downtown and you're just sitting there looking at orange cones for twenty minutes. And the detour signs they put up make absolutely no sense. They route you right through this residential neighborhood where the speed limit is 25, so everyone is just crawling along, and the people who live there are always standing in their yards glaring at the cars like we want to be driving through their street. 

So anyway, I fixed the pipe myself. Sort of. It's still dripping a little bit, but I just stuffed some old towels under there. But, uh, dealing with work? I don't know, man. I don't really think the food helps me deal with anything. It's just... I just eat it, you know? I don't think it's fixing my problems with Dave or the customers.
Do you think eating all that food is a way for you to calm down after a long day at work?

Calm down? I mean, I guess it's kind of like I'm trying to shut my head off. Because most of the time, I'm not even hungry when it starts. Especially if I already ate dinner with my wife. 

Which, by the way, she’s been on this huge kick of making everything in the air fryer lately. We got one for our wedding a few years ago and it just sat in the box in the pantry, but now she uses it for absolutely everything. Chicken, vegetables... she even tried to make chocolate chip cookies in it the other night. They came out like little hockey pucks, I swear. I almost chipped a tooth on one. I actually do need to go to the dentist, now that I think about it. My dental insurance from the grocery store just kicked in, but their network is a complete joke. I looked at the list of approved providers and the closest one is like three towns over, right next to that big shopping mall that went bankrupt. 

You know the one? They turned the old Sears into a massive indoor trampoline park. My nephew had his eighth birthday party there last month and it was pure chaos. Just hundreds of screaming kids and the smell of dirty socks. I don't know how the employees there handle it without losing their minds. The kid at the snack bar looked like he was about to cry when the slushie machine broke. 

But, um... what did you ask me? Calming down after work? Yeah, so, like I was saying, I'm not actually hungry. Even after a full dinner with my wife, I still just end up looking for more food. It's really just... I don't know, like I'm trying to shut my head off.
Do you think eating all that food is a way for you to deal with feelings or emotions that you experience?

Feelings? I mean... I don't really know. I've never really thought about it like that. I'm not exactly sitting there crying into a bag of chips or anything. 

But actually, speaking of crying, my wife was watching this crazy sad movie on Netflix last night. Well, trying to watch it. We kept getting this error message on the TV because Netflix did that whole password crackdown thing recently, right? And my brother-in-law, Gary, he's been using our account for like three years. I told him, Gary, you gotta get your own account now, man. But Gary is incredibly cheap. Like, he refuses to pay for absolutely anything if he can just mooch it. 

He actually still uses a flip phone. A literal flip phone. He claims it's because he doesn't want the government tracking his location, but I know it's just because he doesn't want to pay for a data plan. He works down at the lumber yard and he says the sawdust gets in the smartphones and ruins the screens anyway. Which, I guess makes sense? But still, trying to text the guy is impossible. It takes him ten minutes to type out "okay" because he has to press the buttons three times for every letter. Remember T9 texting? Man, I used to be so fast at that back in high school. I could text under my desk during math class without even looking at the screen. Mr. Henderson never caught me once. 

Wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, emotions. Yeah, I don't really know. I don't think I'm eating because I'm sad or angry or whatever. I haven't really noticed a connection like that. I just... I don't really know why I do it, honestly.
Do you think eating all that food is something you do when you're feeling stressed?

Stressed? I mean... maybe? I guess work can be pretty stressful, but I don't really know if that's the reason. Like, I don't feel a huge wave of stress right before I open the pantry. 

Though, speaking of stress, you should see the new self-checkout lanes they just put in at the grocery store. It's a total nightmare. Corporate decided to replace half the regular registers with these massive machines that constantly yell at people. "Unexpected item in the bagging area!" Over and over, all day long. And the voice on those things is so grating. It sounds exactly like this old GPS unit I used to have. 

Man, I loved that GPS. It was a TomTom, I think. I took it on a road trip down to Florida with my buddies right after we graduated high school. We drove straight through, just taking turns at the wheel of my old Honda Civic. We ended up in Daytona, and the humidity down there was unbelievable. Like walking into a warm wall of soup. We stayed at this really cheap motel that was supposed to have a pool, but the pool was completely empty and filled with wooden ramps. Apparently, the owner's kid was trying to turn it into a skate park. Which is kind of cool, honestly, but we were really looking forward to swimming after being in a car for twenty hours. 

Anyway, my buddy Mike tried to drop in on a skateboard he borrowed from the kid and completely wiped out. Scraped his whole arm up on the concrete. We had to go to a 24-hour pharmacy at like 2 AM to buy bandages and hydrogen peroxide. The cashier there looked like he hadn't slept in a week. He just stared at us the whole time. 

But, uh... wait, what were we talking about? Stress? Yeah, I don't know. I honestly haven't noticed if I eat because I'm stressed out. It's not like I have a bad day with a customer and immediately think, 'I need to go eat.' It just kind of happens when I get home. I don't really see a clear pattern with it, to be honest.
Do you think eating all that food makes you feel better emotionally after a difficult day at work?

Feel better emotionally? I... honestly, I don't think so. I mean, I don't feel great afterward, that's for sure. Usually I just feel stuffed and kind of miserable. 

Speaking of miserable, you should see the break room at work. They finally replaced the old microwave, but the new one they bought is one of those tiny, low-wattage ones. It takes literally six minutes to heat up a frozen burrito. And of course, there's always a line. Yesterday, my coworker, Brenda—she's the one who runs the customer service desk—she put a piece of leftover fish in there. Fish! In a shared microwave! The whole front end of the store smelled like a dock at low tide for the rest of the shift. 

I told my manager, Mr. Peterson, that we needed some air fresheners, but he's super strict about the budget right now. He's this older guy, always wears these really loud, patterned ties. Like, yesterday he had one with little cartoon golf clubs all over it. He's obsessed with golf. He actually tried to get me to join his weekend league last summer, but I told him I don't even own clubs. Plus, my wife wanted to use our weekends to fix up the backyard. 

We tried planting tomatoes, but the squirrels got to every single one of them before they even turned red. We bought this motion-sensor owl to scare them away, but the squirrels literally sit on its head now. It's completely useless. I was reading online that you can spray peppermint oil around the garden to keep them away, but then the whole yard just smells like toothpaste...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask if the food makes me feel better? Yeah, no, it really doesn't. If anything, I feel worse. I just... I don't really know why I keep doing it.
Do you feel like you're in control of how much you eat when you're having those large takeout orders?

Control? No, definitely not. Once I take that first bite, it feels like something in me just clicks off. It's like I'm watching myself do it, and I'm telling myself, 'Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,' but my hands just keep reaching for the next thing. 

It's kind of like... you know when you're driving home from work and you're on autopilot? Like, you pull into your driveway and you don't even remember the last five miles of the drive. I do that all the time. Actually, the other day I was driving home and they had the whole intersection of 4th and Elm blocked off for construction. They've been working on that water main for like six months now. It's ridiculous. The detour took me all the way past the old drive-in theater on the edge of town. Have you seen what they did to that place? They tore down the screen and put up this massive storage unit complex. Who has that much stuff they need to rent a garage just to keep it in? 

My neighbor, Steve, he rents one of those units. He collects vintage arcade cabinets. Like, the full-size ones from the 80s. He's got Pac-Man, Donkey Kong, Asteroids, the whole nine yards. He invited me over to see them once, and it's honestly pretty impressive, but his wife is furious about it. She says they're going to have to take out a second mortgage just to pay for the electricity to keep them all running. Plus, they beep and boop all night long. I can sometimes hear them through the fence if my bedroom window is open. 

Steve's a nice guy, though. He lent me his pressure washer last spring when I was trying to clean off the back patio. Man, those things are powerful. I accidentally got too close to the siding on the house and chipped off a piece of the paint. My wife was not happy about that. I had to go to the hardware store and try to color-match the paint, but the guy at the counter mixed it slightly too yellow. So now there's just this one spot near the back door that looks like it's permanently stained with mustard...

Oh, sorry. Control. Right. Yeah, I don't have any control when I start eating like that. I just can't stop my hands from grabbing the food, even when my brain is telling me to quit.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating when you start with those large takeout orders?

Like I was just saying, man, no. Whether it's how much I'm eating or exactly what I'm eating, the control just isn't there. Once I take that very first bite, it feels like something inside me just clicks off completely. I'll literally be sitting there, in my own head, telling myself, 'Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,' but my hands just keep reaching for the next thing anyway. 

It’s like my brain and my body aren't even connected. Kind of like our Wi-Fi router at home right now. The connection just keeps dropping out of nowhere. We pay for the premium high-speed package, too, but half the time I can't even get a short video to load on my phone. I called the cable company about it last week, and they kept me on hold for an hour and a half. Just listening to that awful elevator music, you know the kind? It loops every thirty seconds. When a guy finally picked up, he told me I needed to unplug the router, wait, and plug it back in. Like I hadn't already tried that ten times! 

Then he said they'd have to send a technician out between 8 AM and 4 PM on a Tuesday. Who can just sit at home all day on a Tuesday? My wife ended up having to take a half-day off work to wait for the guy, and he didn't even show up until 3:45. And you know what he said? He said a squirrel chewed through the coaxial cable outside. Those same squirrels that ruined our tomatoes! I swear, they're out to get me. I'm this close to just getting a big dog that chases them, but our current dog, Buster, is completely useless for that. He's a beagle mix, and he just wants to sleep on the sofa all day. If a squirrel walked right up to him, he'd probably just roll over and ask for a belly rub...

But, uh, yeah. Sorry. What I'm eating. Yeah, no control at all once I start. My hands just keep going no matter what my brain says.
Do you think eating all that food is a way for you to escape or avoid thinking about your problems?

Escape? I mean... yeah, probably. It really is like I’m just trying to shut my head off. Because, honestly, most of the time I’m not even hungry when it starts. Especially if I already ate a full dinner with my wife, you know? 

She’s actually been really into trying new recipes lately. Her sister, Barbara, bought her one of those fancy dual-zone air fryers for her birthday. Barbara is always buying us these crazy kitchen gadgets that take up way too much counter space. Like, last year, she bought us a fondue pot. Who even eats fondue at home anymore? We tried to use it once for New Year's Eve, and the cheese just clumped up into this giant, greasy rubber ball. It took me three days to scrub that pot clean. I actually had to go out to the garage and get a wire brush just to scrape the bottom, and I ended up scratching all the non-stick coating off. My wife was so mad at me. She said I ruined her sister's gift, but honestly, the thing was a total fire hazard anyway. The power cord was barely two feet long, so we had to plug it in right on the edge of the kitchen island, and Buster—our dog—kept walking by and almost tripping on it...

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, avoiding my problems. Yeah. Like I said, even after a big dinner, I still end up looking for more food. It’s definitely not because my stomach is empty. I just... I do it to shut my head off.
Do you think eating all that food is something you do when you feel overwhelmed?

Overwhelmed? I don't know. I haven't really noticed if that's exactly how I'm feeling when it happens. I mean, I get overwhelmed all the time, sure, especially at my job. 

I'm a cashier over at the grocery store on 5th, and they just put in these new self-checkout machines last month. They were supposed to make our jobs easier, but it's a total nightmare. The scanners are super sensitive, so if you even breathe on a barcode twice, it rings the item up twice. Then the little light above the register starts flashing red, and the machine yells "Please wait for assistance" on a loop, and I have to walk over and type in my override code. And the customers get so mad, like it's my fault! 

Just yesterday, this lady was screaming at me because the machine wouldn't take her expired coupon for canned peaches. I tried to tell her, ma'am, the computer literally won't accept it if the date is passed. But she demanded to see the manager. Our manager, Gary, he's completely useless. He just hides in the back office all day. I know he just plays computer games back there because one time I went in to get a new roll of receipt paper and he had it right up on his screen. He didn't even try to minimize the window. He just told me the paper was on the bottom shelf and went back to his game. It's like, I'm out here getting yelled at over fifty cents off canned fruit, and you're just sitting there? Plus, those receipt paper boxes are incredibly heavy. I actually tweaked my shoulder lifting one last week, and it still kind of pops when I reach up to grab the cigarettes from the overhead rack...

But, um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, eating when I'm overwhelmed. Yeah, I really couldn't tell you if that's why I do it. I've just never really connected the two or thought about whether that's the specific feeling I'm having beforehand.
Do you think eating all that food helps you manage or cope with your emotions in any way?

Manage my emotions? I... I really don't know. I honestly haven't noticed if it helps with that or not. I mean, my emotions are always sort of all over the place anyway, especially since we got the new car. 

We finally traded in the old Honda last month. That thing was a death trap. The heater core was completely shot, so in the winter, my wife and I would have to drive to work wearing our heavy winter coats and gloves. And the defroster didn't work either, so I had to keep a little plastic ice scraper right on the dashboard and scrape the inside of the windshield while I was driving. It was terrifying! But the new car, it's a sedan, one of those hybrid ones. It's so quiet, you can't even tell when the engine is on. The first day we had it, I actually left it running in the driveway for like three hours because I thought I turned it off. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, had to come over and knock on the door to tell me. 

Mr. Henderson is always watching everything we do. He’s retired, used to be a postal worker, and now he just sits on his front porch with binoculars. He says he's bird watching, but there are no birds in our neighborhood except for pigeons and those annoying grackles that scream all morning. Last week, he complained to the city because our recycling bin was out on the curb for an extra day. The garbage truck missed our street because of the construction on Elm, and suddenly I'm getting a notice in the mail with a warning fine! Like, come on, man, cut me some slack. I had to call the city sanitation department, and they gave me the complete runaround...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Emotions? Yeah, I don't know. I just haven't really paid attention to whether eating helps me cope with them. It just happens, you know?
Do you think eating all that food helps you feel better when you're upset or anxious?

Feel better? I mean... I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed if it actually makes me feel better when I'm upset. I get anxious a lot, though, especially about money. 

Like, the electric bill just went up again this month. They sent this little insert with the bill explaining the "seasonal rate adjustment," but it's just a bunch of corporate double-talk. They charge you a delivery fee that's higher than the actual electricity you use! I tried calling customer service to ask about it, and I was on hold for forty-five minutes listening to this awful elevator music. It sounded like a synthesizer from the 1980s just playing the same three chords over and over. And then, when a real person finally picked up, the line just clicked and disconnected. I was so mad. I threw my phone on the couch, and it bounced off the cushion and hit Buster right on the nose. 

Poor Buster, he's a good dog, but he's getting old and his eyesight is going. The vet says he has cataracts. We have to put these drops in his eyes twice a day, and it's a two-person job. My wife has to hold his head still while I try to squeeze the bottle, but he wiggles so much. He knocked the bottle out of my hand the other day, and it rolled right under the refrigerator. I had to get down on my hands and knees with a flashlight, and you wouldn't believe the amount of dust bunnies under there. I even found a missing sock that I thought the dryer ate six months ago. It was one of my good wool ones, too, the ones I wear when I have to stand at the register all day because my feet get so cold...

Wait, sorry. I lost my train of thought. What were you asking about? Anxious? Yeah, I just... I couldn't tell you if eating actually helps me feel better. I haven't really paid attention to that part of it.
Do you think eating all that food is a way for you to avoid feeling certain emotions?

Avoid feeling things? I... I don't know. I haven't really thought about it like that, if I'm doing it to avoid anything. I mean, there's a lot I'd like to avoid, mostly my brother-in-law, Steve. 

He just moved into our basement last week because he and his girlfriend broke up. Again. This is the third time this year. He says he just needs a place to crash until he gets back on his feet, but he brought all his stuff. Like, boxes and boxes of it. And he has this massive collection of vintage action figures that he insists on displaying on these floating shelves he drilled into the drywall without asking me. He didn't even use anchors, just screwed them straight into the plaster, and I know they're going to pull right out of the wall the second someone bumps into them. And he stays up all night playing video games online, yelling into his headset. I can hear him through the floor vents in our bedroom. It's like, "Steve, it's 3 AM on a Tuesday, some of us have to be at the grocery store at 7!" 

I tried talking to my wife about it, but she just gets defensive because it's her little brother. She always makes excuses for him, saying he's going through a tough time. But he ate all the good cold cuts I bought for my lunches. I specifically got the honey-glazed turkey from the deli counter, the one they slice real thin, and he just went in there and made himself like three massive sandwiches. Didn't even leave me enough for one. I had to take a can of soup to work, and the microwave in the breakroom is still broken from when Kevin tried to heat up a frozen burrito in the foil wrapper...

Sorry, what was the question? Avoiding emotions? Yeah, I really couldn't say. I just haven't paid attention to whether that's why I'm eating. It's just something that happens.
Do you think eating all that food is a way for you to deal with feelings of emotional distress or upset?

Deal with distress? I honestly... I don't know. I really couldn't tell you if it's about dealing with being upset or not. I just haven't paid that much attention to the why of it. I mean, there's always something upsetting going on, right? Like, just yesterday at the store. 

I was working register four, which is the express lane, fifteen items or less. And this woman comes up with a cart that is completely overflowing. I'm talking easily fifty items. And she starts unloading it on the belt, and I politely pointed to the sign. I said, "Ma'am, this is the express lane, fifteen items or less." And she just glares at me and says, "Well, I'm in a hurry, so you're just going to have to scan fast." I couldn't believe it! And my manager, Brenda, she was right there at the customer service desk, and she didn't do a thing. Brenda never backs us up. She just stands there drinking her iced coffees that she gets from the drive-thru place across the street. She leaves her empty cups all over the breakroom, too. The ice melts and leaves these sticky rings on the tables, and then the ants come. We had an exterminator out twice last month, but they keep coming back because Brenda won't throw her cups in the trash...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Emotional distress? Yeah, I just... I don't know. I really haven't noticed if eating is a way to deal with that. It just happens.

People just sit there in their cars not moving, staring at their phones, and it drives me crazy... but yeah, I'll get all that food and just sit there and eat almost all of it myself before I even go home. I just... I don't really know why I'm doing it.

Manage my emotions? I... I really don't know. I honestly haven't noticed if it helps with that or not. I mean, my emotions are always sort of all over the place anyway, especially since we got the new car. 

We finally traded in the old Honda last month. That thing was a death trap. The heater core was completely shot, so in the winter, my wife and I would have to drive to work wearing our heavy winter coats and gloves. And the defroster didn't work either, so I had to keep a little plastic ice scraper right on the dashboard and scrape the inside of the windshield while I was driving. It was terrifying! But the new car, it's a sedan, one of those hybrid ones. It's so quiet, you can't even tell when the engine is on. The first day we had it, I actually left it running in the driveway for like three hours because I thought I turned it off. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, had to come over and knock on the door to tell me. 

Mr. Henderson is always watching everything we do. He’s retired, used to be a postal worker, and now he just sits on his front porch with binoculars. He says he's bird watching, but there are no birds in our neighborhood except for pigeons and those annoying grackles that scream all morning. Last week, he complained to the city because our recycling bin was out on the curb for an extra day. The garbage truck missed our street because of the construction on Elm, and suddenly I'm getting a notice in the mail with a warning fine! Like, come on, man, cut me some slack. I had to call the city sanitation department, and they gave me the complete runaround...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Emotions? Yeah, I don't know. I just haven't really paid attention to whether eating helps me cope with them. It just happens, you know?

patient.answer:
Feel better? I mean... I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed if it actually makes me feel better when I'm upset. I get anxious a lot, though, especially about money. 

Like, the electric bill just went up again this month. They sent this little insert with the bill explaining the "seasonal rate adjustment," but it's just a bunch of corporate double-talk. They charge you a delivery fee that's higher than the actual electricity you use! I tried calling customer service to ask about it, and I was on hold for forty-five minutes listening to this awful elevator music. It sounded like a synthesizer from the 1980s just playing the same three chords over and over. And then, when a real person finally picked up, the line just clicked and disconnected. I was so mad. I threw my phone on the couch, and it bounced off the cushion and hit Buster right on the nose. 

Poor Buster, he's a good dog, but he's getting old and his eyesight is going. The vet says he has cataracts. We have to put these drops in his eyes twice a day, and it's a two-person job. My wife has to hold his head still while I try to squeeze the bottle, but he wiggles so much. He knocked the bottle out of my hand the other day, and it rolled right under the refrigerator. I had to get down on my hands and knees with a flashlight, and you wouldn't believe the amount of dust bunnies under there. I even found a missing sock that I thought the dryer ate six months ago. It was one of my good wool ones, too, the ones I wear when I have to stand at the register all day because my feet get so cold...

Wait, sorry. I lost my train of thought. What were you asking about? Anxious? Yeah, I just... I couldn't tell you if eating actually helps me feel better. I haven't really paid attention to that part of it.

patient.answer:
Avoid feeling things? I... I don't know. I haven't really thought about it like that, if I'm doing it to avoid anything. I mean, there's a lot I'd like to avoid, mostly my brother-in-law, Steve. 

He just moved into our basement last week because he and his girlfriend broke up. Again. This is the third time this year. He says he just needs a place to crash until he gets back on his feet, but he brought all his stuff. Like, boxes and boxes of it. And he has this massive collection of vintage action figures that he insists on displaying on these floating shelves he drilled into the drywall without asking me. He didn't even use anchors, just screwed them straight into the plaster, and I know they're going to pull right out of the wall the second someone bumps into them. And he stays up all night playing video games online, yelling into his headset. I can hear him through the floor vents in our bedroom. It's like, "Steve, it's 3 AM on a Tuesday, some of us have to be at the grocery store at 7!" 

I tried talking to my wife about it, but she just gets defensive because it's her little brother. She always makes excuses for him, saying he's going through a tough time. But he ate all the good cold cuts I bought for my lunches. I specifically got the honey-glazed turkey from the deli counter, the one they slice real thin, and he just went in there and made himself like three massive sandwiches. Didn't even leave me enough for one. I had to take a can of soup to work, and the microwave in the breakroom is still broken from when Kevin tried to heat up a frozen burrito in the foil wrapper...

Sorry, what was the question? Avoiding emotions? Yeah, I really couldn't say. I just haven't paid attention to whether that's why I'm eating. It's just something that happens.

patient.answer:
Deal with distress? I honestly... I don't know. I really couldn't tell you if it's about dealing with being upset or not. I just haven't paid that much attention to the why of it. I mean, there's always something upsetting going on, right? Like, just yesterday at the store. 

I was working register four, which is the express lane, fifteen items or less. And this woman comes up with a cart that is completely overflowing. I'm talking easily fifty items. And she starts unloading it on the belt, and I politely pointed to the sign. I said, "Ma'am, this is the express lane, fifteen items or less." And she just glares at me and says, "Well, I'm in a hurry, so you're just going to have to scan fast." I couldn't believe it! And my manager, Brenda, she was right there at the customer service desk, and she didn't do a thing. Brenda never backs us up. She just stands there drinking her iced coffees that she gets from the drive-thru place across the street. She leaves her empty cups all over the breakroom, too. The ice melts and leaves these sticky rings on the tables, and then the ants come. We had an exterminator out twice last month, but they keep coming back because Brenda won't throw her cups in the trash...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Emotional distress? Yeah, I just... I don't know. I really haven't noticed if eating is a way to deal with that. It just happens.
